clue.text: Union pay for party and sport

parts.note: an association is a union of people joined for a shared purpose
to foot the bill is to pay for it
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A trade union funds a celebration and a sports event for its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' and 'pay' look like a labour dispute; each word is simply a piece of the answer's spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Association football is the formal name for soccer, the game governed by the Football Association.

clue.text: Job sorting out AI isn't …

indicators.note: sorting things puts them into a new order, so the following letters get rearranged

parts.note: nine letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A worker complains that a job of fixing a broken AI system is not working, the sentence trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's surface to 3 Down; the wordplay is self-contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a post or position of employment, as in 'situations vacant' advertisements.

clue.text: … ours oddly — experts must bring in 50 future consultants?

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd-numbered positions of the preceding word

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: aces are experts at something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Continuing 2 Down: experts need to hire fifty consultants to forecast how things will go.
explanation.walkthrough: The 50 sits between the second and third letters of the experts word. 'Future consultants' is the definition, with a question mark because oracles are consulted about the future rather than being consultants.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles were shrines or priestesses consulted for prophecy, so they are those you consult about what lies ahead.

clue.text: Trick that is used to keep flat in retirement

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for flat is written backwards

parts.note: flat in the sense of dull and lifeless

explanation.surface: A cunning ploy of keeping a flat after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat in retirement' looks like housing for pensioners; it is the word for dull turned backwards, held between the two letters for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Illude is an old verb meaning to deceive or mock, from the same Latin root as illusion.

clue.text: Two classes prepared for printing

parts.note: the first class: a type is a kind or category
the second class: a set is a group of pupils taught together

explanation.surface: Two school classes have been got ready for print, like a yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: two different words that each mean 'class'.
explanation.definitionFit: Typeset text has been arranged in type, ready to go to press.

clue.text: Perhaps Carmen's old fruit hat stripped down to the base

indicators.note: in a down entry the base is the bottom, so that letter is lifted out of the fruit and put at the end

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a common fruit

indicators.note: stripping something removes its outer layer, leaving only the central letter of the word

parts.note: the centre letter, left when the outer two are stripped

explanation.surface: Carmen Miranda's famous old fruit hat, taken apart right down to its foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Carmen Miranda, the singer known for hats piled with fruit. The A already sits inside the fruit; it is moved from there to the bottom of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's opera, so it is an example of the genre, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Subject taught in commercial premises at last

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
at last says where it goes: just before the final letter of the outer word

parts.note: homes are residential premises
economic means relating to trade and commerce

explanation.surface: A business course taught on a company's site, finally.
explanation.walkthrough: The commercial word is inserted at the last position of the premises word, just before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Home economics is a school subject covering cookery, nutrition and household management.

clue.text: Stars produce this type of family animation

parts.note: a nuclear family is parents and their children
animation in the sense of liveliness or vigour

explanation.surface: Celebrities make a lively animated film about a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'animation' suggest film; the stars are the ones in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars shine by nuclear fusion in their cores, releasing nuclear energy as light and heat.

clue.text: See 1
Car manufacturer on power network

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another is placed after it, so the carmaker comes second

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
Lexus is Toyota's luxury car brand

explanation.surface: A carmaker is building a charging network for its electric vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the carmaker follows the power letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plexus is an interwoven network, especially of nerves or blood vessels, as in the solar plexus.

clue.text: Remember playground in its entirety

parts.note: the rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field
all of it, the whole

explanation.surface: Someone tries to remember every detail of a childhood playground.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back into memory.

clue.text: Terribly tiny self-assembly boxes

indicators.note: boxing something encloses it, so the first phrase wraps round the tiny word

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home building and assembly
a direct synonym

explanation.surface: Flat-pack furniture comes in terribly small boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun for the cartons; it is a verb for surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismally means badly or poorly, as in a dismal performance, matching 'terribly'.

clue.text: Block of drugs including speed seized at the start

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the drugs surround the speed word
at the start asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so Es are drugs
a fast pace, as in 'at a fair clip'

explanation.surface: A drug haul including amphetamines is confiscated at the outset of a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' plays on the drug slang but means pace. The initial E goes last, after the drugs-and-speed combination.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to block it from view, as the moon blocks the sun.

clue.text: Ultimately Francis Scott Fitzgerald's right — excellent

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, asking for the final letter of each of the next two names

parts.note: the final letter
the final letter
Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A literary verdict that the Great Gatsby novelist was right and brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads F. Scott Fitzgerald's full name, but the Fitzgerald here is a different one, Ella, and the first two names only lend their last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar literally means of the stars, and informally means outstanding or star-quality.

clue.text: Suspect Brian Lara briefly touring India is one who might quieten the crowd?

definitions.text: one who might quieten the crowd?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the cricketer's surname loses its last letter
touring means going round, so the names surround the letter for India
as an adjective suspect means dubious or not to be trusted, so these letters are not in their real order

parts.note: taken as written
the surname without its final letter
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The great West Indian batsman Brian Lara is under suspicion while on a cricket tour of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Lara is the record-breaking West Indies cricketer. The question mark marks the definition as playful: librarians are known for shushing readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian traditionally keeps a library silent, telling noisy visitors to be quiet.

clue.text: I see grandparent stopping stupidly

indicators.note: stopping a gap means plugging it, so the grandparent fills a space inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
nan is a British informal word for grandmother
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone notices a grandparent coming to a foolish halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb of looking; it is a diocese. The grandparent sits between the I and the see.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanely means in a silly, senseless way, which is what stupidly means.

clue.text: Soap hotel left out working eventually

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the hotel letter is dropped from the soap word

parts.note: lather is the foam soap makes
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A TV soap set in a hotel is dropped from the schedule, though it will eventually be running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soap' suggests a television serial; here it is the foam.
explanation.definitionFit: Later on means at some future time, the same as eventually.

clue.text: Once somebody new pursues terms for North Sea gas worker

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the new letter comes at the end
terms are ends or terminals, asking for the final letter of each of the following three words

parts.note: the last letter of each of the three words
a worker bee
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A former celebrity starts a new career on a North Sea gas rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' is the crossword's usual bee, not a rig hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person who was once famous or important but is no longer.

clue.text: Costume Peter Lorre conclusively wears to horrify

indicators.note: the horrify word puts on these letters like clothing, so it surrounds them

parts.note: to appal is to horrify

indicators.note: conclusively points to the conclusion, the last letter of each of the two names

parts.note: the final letter of each name

explanation.surface: Horror-film actor Peter Lorre puts on a costume to frighten audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Lorre was a Hungarian-born actor famous for sinister roles, which suits the scary surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, and a costume is a set of clothes.

clue.text: Light dessert potentially following meat course's conclusion

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
lamb is a meat

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A light pudding could come after the main meat course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light dessert' reads as a low-calorie pudding; 'light' here means set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé describes food doused in spirit and set alight, as done with crêpes Suzette or Christmas pudding.

clue.text: Degenerate's time inside never to be forgotten

indicators.note: inside places the time letter within the word for degenerate

parts.note: a degenerate person is immoral
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A depraved person's prison term ensures they'll be remembered forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time inside' suggests a jail sentence; it is the T placed in the degenerate word, the 's standing for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortal means living forever, and figuratively whose fame will never fade.

clue.text: Trump exposed party

parts.note: out in the sense of revealed or made public
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Donald Trump exposed as a party to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the politician; it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump someone is to surpass them, as a trump card beats other cards.

clue.text: Dictator's annoyance with journalist reached its highest level

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone who dictates, speaking words out loud for another to write

parts.note: pique is irritation, pronounced like the summit word
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A tyrant's anger with a reporter has reached boiling point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant but means one who says words for someone to transcribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that peaked rose to its maximum point before declining.

clue.text: A&E dressing wound — doctor's stern and more urgently pressing

indicators.note: dressing covers something up, so the letters of A&E wrap round the wound

parts.note: the two letters taken as written
a cut is a wound

indicators.note: a stern is the rear of a ship, so it means the back letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: In a hospital emergency department, a doctor dresses a wound sternly as matters grow more urgent.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, Accident and Emergency, is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means severe and needing urgent attention, so acuter is the comparative, more pressing.

clue.text: Union advice: Uri Geller is a conman performing magic essentially

indicators.note: a performer like a magician puts on an act, so these letters are put through a routine and rearranged

parts.note: eighteen letters taken as written

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so take the central letter of the following word

parts.note: the middle letter of a five-letter word

explanation.surface: A warning that the spoon-bending illusionist Uri Geller is a fraud whose magic is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: Uri Geller is an Israeli-British performer famous for claiming to bend spoons by psychic power.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage counselling is professional guidance for couples, and marriage is a union.
